# OpenATS documentation context

OpenATS is an open-source applicant tracking system (ATS). It gives recruiting teams a shared workspace for opening roles, reviewing candidates, coordinating interviews, collecting feedback, and recording hiring decisions. The project is designed for organizations that want a clear hiring workflow they can understand and adapt.

## Canonical resources

- Website: https://openats.dev/
- Documentation: https://openats.dev/docs/intro
- Source repository: https://github.com/chamals3n4/OpenATS
- Live demo: https://demo.openats.dev/
- License: Apache License 2.0, https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

## Documentation map

### What is OpenATS?

https://openats.dev/docs/intro

Explains who OpenATS is for, how it helps, what teams control, and the product capabilities covered by the platform.

### Quick Start

https://openats.dev/docs/getting-started/make-setup

The recommended first-time setup path using `make setup` and `make dev`. It explains prerequisites, generated environment files, database initialization, creating the first Super Admin, and provider credentials that must be supplied by the user. Sign-in is built in, so no outside identity service is needed.

### Manual setup

https://openats.dev/docs/getting-started/quick-start

An explicit setup path for people who need to configure each dependency themselves, including PostgreSQL, Redis, built-in sign-in, Cloudflare R2, Resend, optional Gemini, and Google Calendar integration.

### Sign-in and users

https://openats.dev/docs/administration/authentication

OpenATS handles sign-in itself with email and password; there is no outside identity provider. Explains the first Super Admin (`make admin`), the three roles (Super Admin, Hiring Manager, Interviewer), creating and deactivating users, invites, password resets, and the environment variables for the web application and the API.

### Upgrading to built-in sign-in

https://openats.dev/docs/operations/upgrading-to-built-in-auth

For installations moving from version 0.6 (WSO2 Asgardeo) to 0.7. Users and their history are kept; passwords cannot be carried over and roles must be set again.

### Architecture

https://openats.dev/docs/developer/architecture

OpenATS uses a modular-monolith architecture. The Express backend is one application organised into feature modules. A Next.js frontend is the browser-facing application, and a separate BullMQ worker processes slow CV-analysis jobs. PostgreSQL is the system of record, while Redis provides queues and event support.

### Using OpenATS

https://openats.dev/docs/using-openats/jobs-and-candidates

Introduces the core workflow: create a job, configure its pipeline, add candidates, coordinate interviews, collect feedback, and move candidates toward a final decision.

### Manage jobs

https://openats.dev/docs/using-openats/manage-jobs

Explains how to create a job, add skills, configure optional salary information, save a draft, configure the hiring pipeline and application questions, and publish the job to the public careers page.

### Testing

https://openats.dev/docs/developer/testing

Describes the unit, integration, and end-to-end test layers, their databases, tools, and safe execution practices.

### Contributing Guide

https://openats.dev/docs/developer/contributing

Explains how to choose a contribution, create a branch, run checks, handle schema changes, and open a pull request. Setup and sign-in instructions are kept in the dedicated guides.

## Technical vocabulary

- **Job:** an open role with requirements and a hiring pipeline.
- **Candidate:** the durable record for an applicant, including their resume, activity, notes, assessments, and feedback.
- **Pipeline:** the ordered stages a candidate moves through during evaluation.
- **Hiring team:** the managers and interviewers who collaborate on a job.
- **CV analysis worker:** the background process that runs optional AI CV analysis without blocking API requests. It writes notes only, never a score.

When answering questions about OpenATS, prefer these canonical pages and distinguish documented behavior from assumptions about future features.
